paragraphs: Tanna de-Vei Eliyahu is not the prophet Elijah but the tanna listed in Maimonides’ introduction to Seder Zera'im, end of chapter 7: Yehoshua ben Perachyah, Nittai the Arbelite, Choni the circle-drawer, Eliyahu. Thus Be'er Sheva, in a responsum and in Chelek 92a. (Shalshelet Hakkabbalah 24b says he was in Yehudah ben Tabbai’s time.) And Einei, Yiven Hikkaf [ועיני יבן היקף; wording unresolved], Yuchasin in Rema’s glosses to Yesod Olam. Mi Shehayah 94a: Tanna de-Vei Eliyahu, Rabbi Natan says, “The whole inhabited world is beneath one star.” Pesachim 112a: Tanna de-Vei Eliyahu, “Though Rabbi Akiva said, Make your Shabbat like a weekday,” etc. If, as Maimonides says, Tanna de-Vei Eliyahu was early, etc., how does he speak in Rabbi Natan’s, Rabbi Akiva’s, and Rabbi Yehudah ben Tema’s names? See there. Moreover, if he was in Rabbi Yehoshua ben Perachyah’s time, 3560 from creation, Zikkukin de-Nura’s wonder grows: Tanna de-Vei Eliyahu says the world lasts six thousand years—two thousand of chaos, two thousand of Torah, two thousand of the messianic era—and because our sins have multiplied, the years that have elapsed have elapsed. At that time it was still 440 years before the beginning of the two thousand messianic years.
